test_intent: Verify that /say with an empty message body sends an empty string via SendMessage.
reason: Mock choreography verifying SendMessage was called with empty string. Low-value edge case: sending empty messages via /say is not a meaningful bot contract. No distinct production behavior worth preserving. The general /say happy path already covers message delivery.

test_intent: Verify that /say correctly forwards messages containing Markdown formatting characters.
reason: Mock choreography verifying SendMessage was called with specific content. The /say command simply passes text through to Telegram's SendMessage with Markdown parse mode; Telegram SDK handles encoding. No distinct bot contract beyond the general happy path. Special character handling is Telegram SDK responsibility, not bot logic.

test_intent: Verify that /send correctly forwards a 1000-character message.
reason: Mock choreography verifying SendMessage was called with long text. No distinct bot contract: Telegram's message length limit (4096 chars) is enforced by the SDK, not bot logic. A 1000-char message is well within limits and behaves identically to any other message. General happy path covers delivery.

test_intent: Verify that /say does not throw when message.Text is null.
reason: DoesNotThrow without outcome assertion is a strong delete signal. Null message text is an unrealistic edge case in production (Telegram always provides text for text messages). No distinct bot contract exists. Defensive programming detail not worth a dedicated test.

test_intent: Verify that /say does not throw when message.From (the user) is null.
reason: DoesNotThrow without outcome assertion is a strong delete signal. In practice, Telegram always provides a From user for messages in group chats. Null user is an unrealistic edge case. No distinct bot contract exists beyond general null-safety, which is not owner-visible.
